subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

He was dismissed for being combative and antagonistic ________ his supervisor.
solution:
The correct answer is **option 4**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct preposition to be used here is **'towards' **
 
• In this statement the appropriate preposition is '**towards**' because other three options don't make any proper sense to the sentence.
 
• The sense of the sentence is asking for a** 'preposition of direction**'. And '**towards'** is to be used as a '**preposition of direction'** here.
 
• Some examples of 'preposition of direction' are
 
 
• **'to', **
 
• **'towards',**
 
• **'over',**
 
• **'near'**
 
 

Hence the correct sentence is '**He was dismissed for being combative and antagonistic towards his supervisor.' **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Sentences with the prepositions given as options are as follow

 
• '**About'** is a **preposition of relation**, and here it doesn't make proper sense. One example of 'about' as preposition is given below

 
 
• My cousin asked me not to worry** about **him
 
 
 
• **'Above'** is p**reposition of place, **and here it doesn't make proper sense. One example of 'above' as preposition is given below
 
 
• There is a mirror **above** the sink 
 
 
 
• '**Through'** is **preposition of direction(one point to the next),** but here it doesn't make proper sense. One example of 'through' as preposition is given below
 
 
• I enjoyed the beauty of kanchanjungha by peeping** through** binoculars.
